topics.title: Early midterm voting begins
topics.summary: Early voting opened in several U.S. states as campaigns focus on prices, trust in elections, foreign policy, and control of Congress.
topics.discussionPrompt: If people vote early because the whole year feels tense, who says that is civic commitment and who says it is just wanting one decision off the table?

topics.title: Hormuz shipping worries grow
topics.summary: Iran said it struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, adding fresh concern for global shipping, oil prices, and naval traffic through a key route.
topics.discussionPrompt: When one narrow stretch of water can shake prices everywhere, who starts checking maps and who starts checking their gas budget?

topics.title: Markets wobble after yield rise
topics.summary: Wall Street ended mixed as bond yields climbed, oil prices swung, and investors weighed inflation pressure after a volatile week.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the market shrugs, dips, and shrugs again in one afternoon, who reads it as strategy and who calls it expensive mood swings?

topics.title: Asia prepares for El Nino
topics.summary: Governments across Asia are expanding heat alerts, water planning, crop measures, and emergency drills ahead of a potentially intense El Nino.
topics.discussionPrompt: If weather planning becomes everyday government work, who feels reassured by the checklists and who wonders why it took this long?

topics.title: Cleaner air linked to toddlers
topics.summary: A long-running New York study linked cleaner air with stronger early childhood development, adding evidence that pollution cuts can help young brains.
topics.discussionPrompt: When cleaner air shows up in toddler development, who celebrates the policy win and who asks what other quiet benefits we have missed?

topics.title: Rivers face global stress
topics.summary: A new Guardian river project highlights drought, pollution, altered flows, and local restoration efforts as freshwater systems face mounting strain.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a river is both infrastructure and a living neighbor, who wants stricter rules and who wants people to fall back in love with it first?

topics.title: Wheat farmers face uncertainty
topics.summary: U.S. wheat farmers are weighing high prices against drought risk, fuel costs, and disrupted global grain trade as weather forecasts stay unsettled.
topics.discussionPrompt: If crop prices rise but everything needed to farm costs more too, who calls it opportunity and who calls it a headache with paperwork?

topics.title: BBC cash reserves shrink
topics.summary: The BBC's public service cash reserves fell sharply after heavy spending, raising questions about future cuts, digital plans, and funding pressure.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a public broadcaster starts watching its savings closely, who worries about quality and who says every institution needs a budget reality check?

topics.title: AI guardrail visions diverge
topics.summary: Reports ahead of U.S.-China talks say both countries want AI guardrails, but they define the biggest risks in very different ways.
topics.discussionPrompt: If two rivals agree on needing rules but disagree on what danger means, who tries finding common ground and who brings extra coffee?

topics.title: South Pole chess draws debate
topics.summary: A planned chess event at the South Pole drew attention for its all-continent ambition and criticism over the travel footprint.
topics.discussionPrompt: If someone stages chess at the South Pole, who loves the weird achievement and who immediately starts calculating the carbon bill?
